title_en: Han Longmei et al. v. Sunshine Life Insurance Co., Ltd., Jiangsu Branch — dispute over insurance contract
ruling_gist_en: Article 17, Paragraph 1 of the Insurance Law of the PRC provides: 'When concluding an insurance contract, the insurer shall explain the terms and contents of the insurance contract to the applicant, and may make inquiries regarding the subject matter of the insurance or the insured's relevant circumstances, and the applicant shall truthfully disclose.' Where the insurer or its authorized agent sells a 'self-service insurance card' without fulfilling the duty to explain, and fails to make inquiries to the applicant on relevant matters, and instead activates the insurance card on behalf of the applicant to form an electronic insurance policy in the form of an electronic data message, after the insurance contract takes effect, the insurer's claim to rescind the insurance contract on the grounds that the contents of the electronic insurance policy are inaccurate and the applicant has violated the duty of truthful disclosure shall not be supported by the people's court.

full_text_en:
Han Longmei et al. v. Sunshine Life Insurance Co., Ltd., Jiangsu Branch — dispute over insurance contract

Ruling Summary

Article 17, paragraph 1 of the Insurance Law provides: "When concluding an insurance contract, the insurer shall explain the terms and conditions of the insurance contract to the applicant, and may make inquiries about the subject matter of the insurance or the relevant circumstances of the insured, and the applicant shall truthfully answer." Where an insurer or its authorized agent sells a "self-service insurance card" without fulfilling the duty of explanation, and fails to make inquiries to the applicant about relevant matters, and instead activates the insurance card on behalf of the applicant to form an electronic insurance policy in the form of an electronic data message, after the insurance contract takes effect, if the insurer claims to rescind the insurance contract on the grounds that the content of the electronic insurance policy is inaccurate and the applicant has violated the duty of truthful disclosure, the people's court shall not support such claim.

Plaintiffs: Han Longmei, female, Han ethnicity, 40 years old, residing at Zhangzhuang Town, Pei County, Jiangsu Province.
Plaintiff: Liu Na, female, Han ethnicity, 19 years old, residing at Zhangzhuang Town, Pei County, Jiangsu Province.
Plaintiff: Liu Kai, male, Han ethnicity, 13 years old, residing at Zhangzhuang Town, Pei County, Jiangsu Province.
Plaintiff: Liu Yuanzhen, male, Han ethnicity, 70 years old, residing at Zhangzhuang Town, Pei County, Jiangsu Province.
Plaintiff: Wang Yuelan, female, Han ethnicity, 69 years old, residing at Zhangzhuang Town, Pei County, Jiangsu Province.

Defendant: Sunshine Life Insurance Co., Ltd., Jiangsu Branch, domiciled at: 3/F, Yihe Commercial Building, No. 68 Shanxi Road, Gulou District, Nanjing.
Person in charge: Chu Liang, Deputy General Manager of the Company.

The plaintiffs Han Longmei, Liu Na, Liu Kai, Liu Yuanzhen, and Wang Yuelan filed an action with the Gulou District People's Court of Nanjing, Jiangsu Province, against the defendant Sunshine Life Insurance Co., Ltd., Jiangsu Branch (hereinafter referred to as Sunshine Life) over a dispute concerning an insurance contract.

The plaintiffs Han Longmei, Liu Na, Liu Kai, Liu Yuanzhen, and Wang Yuelan alleged: In March 2009, Liu Ji, the son of Liu Yuanzhen and Wang Yuelan, the husband of Han Longmei, and the father of Liu Na and Liu Kai, purchased a "Brilliant Sunshine" type insurance policy launched by the defendant Sunshine Life, with an insurance amount of RMB 60,000 and an insurance term of one year. On April 20, 2009, Liu Ji died in a traffic accident while on his way to Sichuan. The five plaintiffs, all being the legal heirs of Liu Ji, filed a claim for compensation with Sunshine Life in accordance with the law but were unreasonably refused. The plaintiffs requested the court to order Sunshine Life to pay insurance proceeds of RMB 60,000 as agreed and to bear the litigation costs of this case.

The defendant Sunshine Life defended: Our company deeply sympathizes with the unfortunate death of Liu Ji in the traffic accident, and we have no objection to the fact that the five plaintiffs are the heirs of Liu Ji. However, the "Brilliant Sunshine" type insurance involved in this case, launched by our company, adopts the form of an "electronic policy" to conclude the insurance contract. The entire application process is conducted using electronic data messages. The process of activating the electronic policy is the process by which the insurer makes inquiries and explains to the applicant. During the process when the applicant logs into the Sunshine Life website to fill in relevant information, the insurer, through the design of the online system's application process, fulfills its duty to explain the insurance content in accordance with the law and also makes inquiries on certain issues, such as requiring the applicant to truthfully state his occupation and fully providing all insurable options (e.g., "farmer") for the applicant to choose and make a truthful disclosure. If Liu Ji had truthfully disclosed his occupation, i.e., "commercial truck driver," the system would have rejected the insurance. Given that Liu Ji intentionally failed to fulfill his duty of truthful disclosure by making a false statement by selecting "farmer" as his occupation to conclude the insurance contract with our company, our company has the right to rescind the insurance contract, and for the insured event occurring before the rescission of the contract, our company shall not bear liability for compensation or payment of insurance proceeds, nor shall it refund the insurance premium. In summary, the plaintiffs' claims should be dismissed.

The Gulou District People's Court of Nanjing, Jiangsu Province found the following facts after trial:

The "Brilliant Sunshine" insurance card is a self-service insurance card sold by the defendant Sunshine Life in its short-term personal comprehensive accidental injury insurance business and is activated online. The front of the insurance card is printed with: "Insurance coverage: Accidental death and disability benefit of RMB 60,000, accidental injury medical benefit of RMB 10,000; insurance term: 1 year, premium: RMB 100, self-service insurance card series and card number." The back of the card reads: "Account number, password, activation valid until June 30, 2010 (please activate before this date); activation methods: online activation: log in to Sunshine Insurance Group website www.ygbx.com — click on 'Activate Online' page — enter account number, password, verification code to enter the insurance page — fill in relevant insurance information — confirm activation success. Telephone activation: call Sunshine Insurance National Customer Service Hotline 95510, select life insurance, after the agent answers, provide insurance information, confirm activation success." The insurance card promotional brochure provides detailed introductions to the product's coverage content, insured persons, premiums and share limits, precautions, insurance application regulations, insurance coverage, exclusions, claim guidelines, etc., and excerpts some insurance clauses. Among them, Article 1 of the "Important Tips" section states that the insurance card is for customer insurance application only and is not an insurance certificate. The cardholder must apply for insurance according to the insurance process within the validity period of the card. After obtaining the policy number, the insurance coverage corresponding to the card shall take effect at 00:00 of the day following activation. Article 6 of the "Insurance Application Regulations" provides that for insurance application, only persons in occupational categories 1, 2, 3, and 4 are accepted as insureds; persons in occupational categories above 4 are not accepted as insureds. The occupational categories are determined according to the Occupational Classification Table of Sunshine Life Insurance Co., Ltd. Article 1.2 of the Sunshine Life Personal Comprehensive Accidental Injury Insurance Clauses (filed with the China Insurance Regulatory Commission in June 2008), separately provided by the insurer, stipulates that this contract shall take effect from the date when the company agrees to underwrite, collects the insurance premium, and issues the insurance certificate. Article 6.1 of the insurance clauses provides that when concluding this contract, the company will clearly explain the terms and conditions of this contract to the applicant, especially the exclusion clauses. The company will make written inquiries about the relevant circumstances of the applicant and the insured, and the applicant and the insured shall truthfully answer. The insurance clauses do not contain any provisions on the occupation of the insured. The insurance clauses and the promotional brochure do not record the Occupational Classification Table of Sunshine Life Insurance Co., Ltd. The Sunshine Life website allows access to the Occupational Classification Table of Sunshine Life Insurance Co., Ltd. Through the webpage setup, during the activation process of the insurance card, the insurance company makes inquiries on various issues including the insured's occupation, and provides options for insurable occupations for the insured, requiring the applicant to answer by filling in or selecting. This occupational classification table lists commercial truck drivers under the sixth major category: production, transportation equipment operators and related personnel. During the online activation process, if "commercial truck driver" is selected in the insured's occupation column, the insurance card cannot be activated due to rejection of underwriting, and no electronic policy can be formed.

On December 5, 2008, the defendant Sunshine Life entered into an insurance agency contract with Xuzhou Minxing Insurance Agency Co., Ltd. (hereinafter referred to as Minxing Agency), stipulating that Minxing Agency would act as an agent for Sunshine Life's insurance sales business in the Xuzhou area, with a contract term of one year.

Liu Ji was an agricultural household registrant, owner of a Jiefang brand truck with license plate Su CB8375. On November 27, 2006, he obtained a road transport permit for operating motor vehicles for business activities for this vehicle. Liu Ji's driving license indicated that he was qualified to drive Category B vehicles.

In March 2009, Liu Ji purchased one "Brilliant Sunshine" insurance card from Zong Qin, a salesperson of Minxing Agency, for RMB 100. The Sunshine Life website system showed that the insurance card purchased by Liu Ji had been activated, with his occupation listed as farmer, the insured as Liu Ji, the insurance coverage period from 00:00 on March 16, 2009 to 24:00 on March 15, 2010, and the policy did not designate a beneficiary.

On April 20, 2009, Liu Ji was involved in a traffic accident while driving the Jiefang brand truck with license plate Su CB8375 in Sichuan. The next day, Liu Ji died despite rescue efforts at the hospital.

The five plaintiffs in this case, namely Han Longmei (wife of Liu Ji), Liu Na (daughter), Liu Kai (son), Liu Yuanzhen (father), and Wang Yuelan (mother), are all legal heirs of Liu Ji. The five plaintiffs filed a claim for compensation with the defendant Sunshine Life. On June 15, 2009, Sunshine Life issued a written notice of rejection to the five plaintiffs, stating that Liu Ji had applied for insurance with the occupation of farmer, but his actual occupation was "commercial truck driver," and based on the excluded occupations listed in the "Brilliant Sunshine" insurance card, a decision to reject the claim was made.

During the proceedings, the five plaintiffs applied for Zong Qin, a salesperson of Minxing Agency, to testify as a witness. Witness Zong Qin testified: I am a salesperson of Minxing Agency, and I did not know Liu Ji before. In March 2009, I went to Liu Ji's village to conduct insurance promotion and promoted the "self-service insurance card." Liu Ji purchased a "Brilliant Sunshine" insurance card and immediately paid the relevant premium of RMB 100. According to company regulations, when selling insurance, I as a salesperson did not carry the insurance card with me. After collecting the premium, I handed it over to the company, and the company's internal staff activated the insurance card on behalf of the insured based on the salesperson's statement about the insured's occupation. I thought that since the village was all farmers and Liu Ji was also a farmer, I did not ask about his occupation and reported his occupation as "farmer" to the company. A few days later, I delivered the activated insurance card to Liu Ji.

The above facts are confirmed by the following evidence provided by the five plaintiffs: notice of rejection, traffic accident identification certificate, certificate of household registration cancellation, autopsy analysis opinion, death certificate, identity certificates of the plaintiffs, witness testimony; and evidence provided by the defendant Sunshine Life: insurance clauses, insurance card, online activation process description, query results, vehicle driving permit, certificate from the vehicle management office, etc. The evidence is sufficient to establish the facts.

The disputed issues in this case are: whether the defendant Sunshine Life fulfilled its duty to explain the terms and conditions of the insurance contract, and whether Liu Ji violated the applicant's duty of truthful disclosure.

The Gulou District People's Court of Nanjing, Jiangsu Province is of the opinion that:

Article 17, paragraph 1 of the Insurance Law of the People's Republic of China (hereinafter referred to as the Insurance Law) provides: "When concluding an insurance contract, the insurer shall explain the terms and conditions of the insurance contract to the applicant, and may make inquiries about the subject matter of the insurance or the relevant circumstances of the insured, and the applicant shall truthfully answer." With respect to the applicant's duty of disclosure, in addition to the provisions of Article 17, paragraph 1 of the Insurance Law, the insurance clauses provided by the defendant Sunshine Life itself also provide: "When concluding this contract, the company will make written inquiries about the relevant circumstances of the applicant and the insured, and the applicant and the insured shall truthfully answer." It can be seen that the scope of the applicant's duty of disclosure shall be limited to the matters inquired about by the insurer. For matters not inquired by the insurer, the applicant does not bear the duty of disclosure.

In this case, witness Zong Qin testified that at the time of collecting the insurance premium, she mistakenly believed that Liu Ji was a farmer and did not ask about his occupation. The insurance card in question was activated by the insurance agency on behalf of the insured based on the salesperson's statement about the insured's occupation, and was later delivered to Liu Ji. Given that Zong Qin, as the person who handled the sale of the defendant Sunshine Life's insurance business to Liu Ji, has an interest in the matter with Sunshine Life, her testimony unfavorable to Sunshine Life is highly credible. Moreover, Sunshine Life failed to adduce evidence to prove that the insurance card in question was activated by Liu Ji himself, and also failed to adduce evidence to prove that it made a written inquiry about Liu Ji's occupation at the time of collecting the insurance premium. Therefore, it can be determined that Sunshine Life failed to fully fulfill its duty to explain the terms and conditions of the insurance contract.

The occupational classification table for the insured can be accessed on Sunshine Life's website. During the online activation process, if "commercial truck driver" is selected in the insured's occupation column, the insurance card cannot be activated due to rejection of underwriting. However, the insurance card in this case was activated by the internal staff of Minxing Agency on behalf of the insured. During the activation process, Minxing Agency only made inquiries to its salesperson Zong Qin, but did not make inquiries to the applicant Liu Ji. Zong Qin did not inquire about Liu Ji's occupation, so Liu Ji had no opportunity to fulfill his duty of truthful disclosure regarding his occupation. Therefore, Liu Ji did not violate the applicant's duty of truthful disclosure. Sunshine Life's claim that Liu Ji violated the duty of disclosure and its request to rescind the contract and be exempted from corresponding compensation liability have no factual or legal basis. Therefore, the insurance contract in question is valid and effective, with the insurance coverage period from 00:00 on March 16, 2009 to 24:00 on March 15, 2010. On April 20, 2009, Liu Ji died accidentally in a traffic accident, which constitutes an insured event. The insurer shall bear compensation liability in accordance with the insurance contract.

Article 64 of the Insurance Law provides: "After the death of the insured, under any of the following circumstances, the insurance proceeds shall be treated as the insured's estate, and the insurer shall perform the obligation of paying the insurance proceeds to the insured's heirs: (1) where no beneficiary is designated; ..." In this case, the insurance contract in question did not designate a beneficiary. The plaintiffs Han Longmei, Liu Na, Liu Kai, Liu Yuanzhen, and Wang Yuelan, as the legal heirs of Liu Ji, have the right to demand that Sunshine Life perform the obligation to pay the insurance proceeds.

Accordingly, the Gulou District People's Court of Nanjing, Jiangsu Province rendered the following judgment on November 20, 2009:

The defendant Sunshine Life shall pay insurance proceeds of RMB 60,000 to the plaintiffs Han Longmei, Liu Na, Liu Kai, Liu Yuanzhen, and Wang Yuelan.

After the first-instance judgment was pronounced, neither party filed an appeal within the statutory period. The first-instance judgment has become legally effective.
